newsitem.title: INDIA: India money market shifting focus to term money.
newsitem.headline: India money market shifting focus to term money.

text.p: Indian call money was steady at 0.10-0.25 in latest morning deals on Friday, dealers said.
Three-day money opened up at 1.50-2.00 percent, they said.
"The rates (for three-day money) are only quotes and no deals have been reported," one dealer said. "Most of the deals are likely to be in the range of 0.75-1.00 percent," he said.
The market started diverting interest from the call money market to the emerging term money market, dealers said.
Thirty-day money was quoted in the 3.0-4.0 percent range, while the three-months deals were struck by private banks at 8.25 percent to 9.0 percent, dealers said.

The securities market witnessed a selling interest in the short-term and long-term maturity paper in the opening session, dealers said. "The rates are quoted ten basis points below previous traded prices," a dealer said.
In latest trades, the 13.50 percent government stock 1997 was traded at 102.26 rupees against the previous close of 102.38 rupees, he said.
